name: False crashes
formula: count(runs killed-at-cap but waiting) / count(non-done runs)
purpose: How often runs are killed prematurely while merely waiting.
description: Runs killed at the recovery cap that were actually just waiting.
how_to_read: Low-N today. Pair the count with a 'why' drill to see whether the recovery cap is firing on healthy waits.

name: Interruptions
formula: count(Stop) / count(UserPromptSubmit) from the event stream
purpose: How much the human keeps stepping in — the babysitting signal.
description: Stop events ÷ UserPromptSubmit events.
how_to_read: High means the human keeps stepping in. Read as the babysitting signal for autonomy health.

name: Project health
formula: each active metric's latest daily value normalized to [0,1] by its direction, combined by metrics.weight, ×100
purpose: The 'is this project healthy?' glance — a summary of FTR and its companions.
description: A single 0–100 roll-up of the project's active metrics.
how_to_read: Drill into the components to see what's dragging it. Not a substitute for FTR — a summary of it and its companions.

name: Cost per result
formula: subscription fee over the trailing 30 days / (merged runs + accepted recommendations) in the same window
purpose: What a delivered result actually costs — the only money question a flat subscription can answer.
description: Subscription fee for the trailing 30 days divided by what shipped in it (merged runs + accepted recommendations).
how_to_read: Read with throughput: this falls when you ship more for the same fee, so a drop is genuine efficiency. It is NOT a token metric — under a subscription the marginal cost of a token is zero, so tokens per day measure context consumed, not money. Blank until you configure your plan.

name: Memory promotion
formula: count(memories created) / count(eligible patterns+corrections)
purpose: Whether the measure→distill→govern loop is closing — is sensei learning?
description: Memories created ÷ eligible patterns/corrections (instance_count ≥ 3).
how_to_read: ≈0 is the signal — it proves the distill loop is silent. Watch for a flatline at 0 as a loop-health alert.

name: Context pressure
formula: count(sessions with a context-pressure trouble signal) / count(measurable sessions) over the window
purpose: How often sessions run into context limits — a signal that work is outgrowing a single session.
description: Share of measurable sessions that hit context pressure (compaction / low-context or start-fresh advice).
how_to_read: A rising rate means sessions are hitting compaction or low-context warnings before finishing — lean on smaller tasks or checkpoints. Read paired with FTR and time-to-useful-result: pressure that doesn't hurt FTR is tolerable.

name: First-turn resolution
formula: count(sessions where ftr=true) / count(sessions) over the window
purpose: The north-star outcome signal — everything is judged by whether it moves FTR.
description: Share of sessions completed without a correction turn.
how_to_read: Never read alone — a high FTR with rising rework means work is being deferred, not done. Companion: rework share. Friction concentrates in big multi-surface repos, so always drill to per-module FTR.

name: Rework share
formula: Σ tool_calls in sessions where outcome='corrected' / Σ tool_calls
purpose: FTR's mandatory companion — shows how much effort goes into fixing rather than building.
description: Share of all tool-calls that came from corrected sessions.
how_to_read: Raw volume is an inverted productivity signal (8 of the top-10 sessions by volume are the worst). High and rising means effort is going into fixing, not building. Read with FTR.

name: Run completion
formula: count(runs status='done') / count(runs)
purpose: Autonomy health — how often runs finish on their own.
description: Autonomous runs reaching done ÷ runs started.
how_to_read: Low-N today — gate the display until enough runs. Read as autonomy health.

name: Spec depth
formula: mean over scored sessions of the 0-5 spec-depth judgment (transcript-internal plan), per repository per day
purpose: Did the session plan deeply before building? An LLM judgment over the transcript's own stated plan — the upstream driver of first-try success.
description: How complete/observable the plan stated in a session's opening turns was before implementation began (acceptance criteria, inputs/outputs/deps, no TBDs).
how_to_read: Only sessions with a plan-like opening are scored; ad-hoc sessions are N/A (excluded), so read it as 'of the sessions that planned, how deep'. Grounded in quoted plan turns; read paired with FTR + deviation.

name: Spec deviation
formula: planned sessions flagged as deviating / planned sessions, per repository per day
purpose: Did the work stay true to the plan? Deviation is where scope creep and rework originate.
description: Share of planned sessions whose implementation departed from the stated plan (unplanned scope, instead-of-X pivots, dropped plan items).
how_to_read: Denominator is sessions that had a stated plan (others N/A). Some deviation is healthy discovery; read the trend paired with FTR + rework, and open the evidence pairs (plan quote vs deviating action) before judging.

name: Churn concentration
formula: Σ churn(top 20% files) / Σ churn(all files)
purpose: Whether a few hotspots absorb most of the rework — the files to refactor first.
description: Share of churn from the busiest 20% of files (Pareto).
how_to_read: Neutral in isolation; actionable as a target list. High concentration points to the hotspot files to refactor first.

name: Churn rate
formula: count(process_file task_executions) per file per day
purpose: How much code is being rewritten — GitClear's churn definition, measured first-party.
description: process_file executions/day per source file (reverted-or-rewritten proxy).
how_to_read: Pair with duplication. Inflated by the version-rescan bug until debounced, so de-noise before trending.

name: Coverage
formula: Σ lines hit (LH) / Σ lines found (LF) from the ingested lcov report
purpose: How much of the code the tests exercise — the safety net behind AI-assisted change.
description: Covered source lines ÷ instrumented source lines, from an lcov report the project's test run produced.
how_to_read: Higher is better. Lines hit (LH) ÷ lines found (LF) from an lcov report INGESTED from the current checkout (the daemon never runs your tests). No report → no row until your test run / CI writes one at a known path (or set metrics.coverage_lcov). A present-tense snapshot; historical coverage is the opt-in backfill (checkout past commits + run the coverage command). scope=repo (whole-suite, never per-author).

name: Duplication
formula: Σ duplicated lines (qlty smells) / total source lines (qlty metrics) at the commit as-of the sampled day
purpose: DRY erosion over real history — the code-duplication signal, measured by qlty over a git worktree at each sampled commit.
description: Duplicated source lines ÷ total source lines, from a qlty scan at each sampled commit.
how_to_read: Rising duplication means DRY erosion. Duplicated lines (qlty smells) ÷ total source lines (qlty metrics) at a git worktree checked out to each sampled commit-day, so it backfills over real git history (superseding the earlier own-graph symbol snapshot). Sampled ~weekly to bound scan cost; a commit before qlty was configured, a non-git project, or an absent qlty CLI → no row (honest-empty, never a fabricated score). History rows are project-level; per-module (folder) attribution is a deferred follow-up.

name: Shallow analysis
formula: sessions with >=1 understanding-retraction / measurable sessions, per repository per day
purpose: Building before understanding, detected semantically — the LLM companion to the deterministic edit before read signal.
description: Share of sessions showing a retraction-of-understanding ('I misread', 'let me actually check', 're-read') that the deterministic edit before read signal can't see.
how_to_read: Read alongside edit before read (the deterministic proxy): the two together triangulate 'dived in before analysis'. Evidence = the retraction turn. Heuristic, not intent.

name: Edit before read
formula: sessions whose first edit precedes any read/search (or that edit with no read at all) / sessions with >=1 edit, per repository per day
purpose: Process-quality proxy: did the session explore before editing? The deterministic first slice of the transcript process-quality signals.
description: Share of code-editing sessions that modified a file before any read or search — a proxy for building before understanding.
how_to_read: A heuristic from tool-event ordering, not intent — brand-new files or trivial known tweaks can inflate it. Read the trend, not a single day; high + rising alongside rework suggests diving in before analysis.

name: Maintainability
formula: count(qlty maintainability smells) / total source lines (qlty metrics) at the commit as-of the sampled day
purpose: Code maintainability over real history — the complexity/structure smell burden, measured by qlty over a git worktree at each sampled commit.
description: Maintainability-smell burden ÷ total source lines, from a qlty scan at each sampled commit.
how_to_read: Higher means more maintainability smells per line (file/function complexity, deep nesting, long parameter lists) — lower is better. qlty's structural smell findings ÷ total source lines at a git worktree checked out to each sampled commit-day; sampled ~weekly to bound scan cost. Coverage is NOT part of this metric — a historical worktree has no coverage artifact, so coverage stays honest-empty (never fabricated). History rows are project-level; per-module (folder) attribution is a deferred follow-up.

name: Refuted findings
formula: sessions with >=1 self-refuted finding / measurable sessions, per repository per day
purpose: Self-correction churn: how often the assistant's own conclusions flipped mid-session — a signal of shaky analysis.
description: Share of sessions where the assistant asserted a finding it later reversed itself (distinct from a user correction).
how_to_read: Not the same as user corrections (that's rework/FTR); this is the assistant refuting itself. A little is normal exploration. Evidence pairs the assertion turn with the retraction turn.

name: Rework density
formula: count(files in detected_patterns rework:) / count(project files)
purpose: Where correction-proneness lives — the per-module friction map.
description: Files flagged rework: ÷ project files.
how_to_read: Multi-surface repos concentrate it. Read as the per-module friction map to locate where rework clusters.

name: Tools used
formula: count(tools with 0 outcome-positive calls in 14d)
purpose: Dead surface area — tooling that is registered but never used.
description: Registered tools with 0 successful outcomes in the window.
how_to_read: Report as a single aggregate ('40 tools dormant'), never one card per tool.

name: Context reuse
formula: mean over sessions of (cache_read / (fresh_input + cache_write + cache_read)), per repository per day
purpose: Whether sessions run long enough to reuse their context, or keep re-paying for it.
description: Mean share of a session's input tokens served from cache rather than re-sent fresh.
how_to_read: Averaged per SESSION, not per request — per request it is a flat 99.8% because the prefix is cached on nearly every call. The spread comes from session LENGTH: long sessions sit at 96-99%, 2-3 turn sessions fall to ~83%, because a short session never amortises its cold start. A low value means many short sessions re-paying for context they could have reused. Read with session duration.

name: Input tokens per day
formula: sum(tokens_in) over sessions with token usage, per repository per day
purpose: How much context the models processed — the input side of token volume.
description: Input tokens processed per day (raw prompt + cache creation + cache reads).
how_to_read: Largely cache re-reads that grow with session length; a spike usually means longer sessions or heavier context, not necessarily waste. Compare against output tokens for the input/output balance.

name: Output tokens per day
formula: sum(tokens_out) over sessions with token usage, per repository per day
purpose: The generation side of token volume — closest proxy for how much the models produced.
description: Output tokens generated per day (the model's actual generation, incl. reasoning).
how_to_read: Not inflated by input cache, so a cleaner 'work produced' signal than input tokens. Read alongside throughput: more output for the same delivered work can mean verbosity or rework.

name: Tokens per day
formula: sum(tokens_in + tokens_out) over sessions with token usage, per repository per day
purpose: Overall token volume — how heavy the day's AI usage was.
description: Total model tokens (input incl. cache + output) consumed per day.
how_to_read: A volume/cost signal, not a quality one. Read the trend, not a single day: rising tokens with flat throughput can mean heavier context or more rework. Dominated by input cache re-reads on long sessions.

name: Tokens per result
formula: sum(tokens_out over completed sessions) / count(completed sessions), per repository per day
purpose: Efficiency / cost-per-result — is delivered work getting leaner or heavier in tokens.
description: Output tokens generated per completed session — the token cost of a delivered result.
how_to_read: Read paired with throughput + FTR: cheap-but-wrong is not value, and a big feature legitimately costs more tokens. A rising median means results are getting more token-expensive. Output-based, so not inflated by input cache re-reads.

name: Session duration
formula: avg(active duration seconds) over sessions with a recorded duration, per repository per day
purpose: How long sessions ran — the effort/time dimension alongside token volume.
description: Average active working time per session (gap-aware, excludes long idle gaps).
how_to_read: Descriptive, not good/bad: a long session that delivered a big feature is fine. Read the trend paired with throughput + tokens. This is active work time, not wall-clock.

name: Throughput
formula: count(sessions) per day
purpose: How much work is being completed per day.
description: Completed sessions per day (and, later, features/day).
how_to_read: Only meaningful paired with FTR — throughput of corrected work is negative value. Never report LOC or edit-count as velocity.

name: Time to useful result
formula: median over sessions of ((first turn where is_correction=false).ended_at - session.started_at), per day
purpose: Latency / speed-to-value — the one signal FTR (a rate) and throughput (a count) don't capture.
description: Median seconds from session start to the first non-correction turn — how fast a session produced its first usable output.
how_to_read: Read paired with FTR: fast-but-wrong is not value. A rising median means the first usable output is taking longer. Idle time between turns can inflate it.
